summary: Niger keeps its doors open to West African neighbors — ECOWAS-origin citizens still enter visa-free after the country's 2025 exit from the bloc, as do Chad, Mauritania, Morocco and Tunisia, and Hong Kong passport holders for up to 14 days; UAE citizens can get a visa on arrival, but nearly every other nationality must obtain a visa from a Nigerien embassy before travel, against a backdrop of junta rule and do-not-travel security advisories.

passportValidity.text: Your passport should be valid for the proposed duration of your stay. No additional period of validity is required.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Niger entry requirements

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: Niger requires proof of yellow fever vaccination from all arriving travelers aged 9 months and over.

source.name: WHO, International Travel and Health, Annex 1 — countries requiring proof of vaccination against yellow fever
source.instrument: International Health Regulations (2005), Article 36 and Annex 7; WHO International Travel and Health, Annex 1, 18 November 2022 (revised 3 January 2023)

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for visitors to Niger. The UK Foreign Office says medical facilities are poor, even in Niamey, that serious treatment would need evacuation to Europe, and advises adequate travel health insurance and accessible funds.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Niger travel advice: health

onwardTicket.text: No official source we could read states an onward- or return-ticket requirement for Niger.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Niger

proofOfFunds.text: No official source we could read states a proof-of-funds requirement or amount for Niger.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Niger

notes: Photographing military sites, checkpoints, airports and government buildings is prohibited and taken seriously. Ask before pointing a camera at anything official.
Satellite phones and drones can require prior authorization. Check with a Nigerien embassy before bringing either.

payments.text: Niger runs on cash. Cards are accepted at a couple of Niamey hotels at best, and ATMs that take foreign cards are scarce even in the capital. Bring euros to change and keep small XOF notes for daily spending.

safety.text: The FCDO advises against all travel to Niger because of terrorist attacks and the kidnapping of foreign nationals, a risk throughout the country including Niamey, and the political situation remains unstable after the July 2023 military coup. Foreign nationals may travel outside Niamey only with the government's permission and an escort of Nigerien security and military forces. Gunfire was reported near the Presidential Palace and Niamey airport on 29 August 2026.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Niger travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to February is the cooler dry season — the only comfortable months. From March to May temperatures in Niamey and the Sahel routinely exceed 45°C.

idp.text: Niger is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Geneva, 19 September 1949 (UNTS vol. 125, p. 3); Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

driving.text: Niger is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Niger yet.

tips.text: Most governments advise against all travel to Niger. If you must go, arrange security guidance in advance, keep movements low-profile and register with your embassy — several Western embassies now operate with reduced staff.
Do not plan overland arrivals — the borders with Burkina Faso, Mali and Libya cross active conflict zones and land crossings open and close without notice. Fly into Niamey.
Never photograph checkpoints, soldiers, airports or government buildings. Detentions over photos are a recurring problem for foreigners.
Bring enough cash (euros are easiest to change) for your whole stay. Cards and foreign-card ATMs are close to useless outside one or two Niamey hotels.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Niger?
faq.answer: Citizens of ECOWAS-origin West African states, plus Chad, Mauritania, Morocco and Tunisia, enter visa-free, and Hong Kong passport holders can stay up to 14 days without a visa. UAE ordinary-passport holders can obtain a visa on arrival. Everyone else — including EU, UK and US passport holders — must obtain a visa from a Nigerien embassy or consulate before travel; there is no eVisa or visa on arrival for them.

faq.question: Is it safe to travel to Niger right now?
faq.answer: Most Western governments advise against all travel to Niger due to terrorism, kidnapping and the unstable political situation following the 2023 coup. Tourist travel to the Sahara circuits (Agadez, Aïr, Ténéré) has been effectively suspended for years. Check your government's latest advisory before making any plans.

faq.question: Did Niger's exit from ECOWAS end visa-free travel for West Africans?
faq.answer: No. Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso formally left ECOWAS in January 2025, but both sides have maintained visa-free movement. The AES states announced ECOWAS citizens may still enter without a visa, and ECOWAS reciprocates. Arrangements could change, so check before traveling.

faq.question: Is yellow fever vaccination mandatory for Niger?
faq.answer: Yes — Niger requires a yellow fever vaccination certificate from all arriving travelers aged 9 months and over, whatever country you arrive from.

faq.question: Can French citizens get a visa for Niger?
faq.answer: Relations between Niger's military government and France broke down after the 2023 coup, and visa issuance to French nationals has been suspended or heavily restricted since. French citizens should contact the nearest Nigerien mission for the current position before planning travel.
